items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: I once proposed to her... But she was already a star and I didn't really know her.

ctx.x: Yeah, he's the guy that hangs around, the kind that asks 'you where you're going from here'. This lady, for that was and Chu Berry's answer / 'straight up.' (Laughter.)

Well, you know Duke wrote a tune that I heard in Sacramento in 1933, and I still remember, it's the only time I ever heard it, and the words were, 'I don't finance romancers, I don't romance financiers, I just take things slow and easy, dry long so. So finally I asked Cootie that, five years ago I said, this song -- Ivy Anderson, he got very upset. 'That was my song, I sang it.' I said, well, the night I heard it, she sang it. I said, what the hell does 'dry long so', I don't even know how you spell it, even. He…
Oh, yes, that's a black expression.
